correctness.rationale: Stationary cycle-length bias gives \(\psi(dv)=\phi(dv)/[v\int\phi(du)/u]\), independently of uniform position on \((0,L)\). At lags \(0<t<a/v_+\), a path initially above the detector cannot reset. Thus \(H_a(t)=L^{-1}\int(L-a-vt)_+\,\psi(dv)\). The transform with \(z=(L-a)/t\) has distributional second derivative \(K^{\prime\prime}=\psi\) on \(z>z_0\). Equality of observed potentials is equivalent to upper-tail agreement and equality of mass and first moment in the unobserved lower interval. At \(z_0\le v_-\) all mass, including endpoint atoms, is identifiable. For \(z_0>v_-\), signed smooth perturbations with vanishing zeroth and first moments establish distinct positive continuous laws with identical data. A standalone checker confirms 293 exact-rational examples; finite tests do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The physically motivated inverse problem is complete: a one-bit stationary spatial detector compensates for a universal uninformative one-time density and recovers an unrestricted Borel speed law precisely when its location exceeds an explicit contrast-dependent threshold. Below the threshold the theorem states exactly what is and is not identifiable and gives genuinely different smooth-law witnesses. This is a sharp sensor-design boundary, not a generic numerical increment or unsituated moment.
